text:
Build a restaurant
that is easier to run
POS + Odoo ERP designed around your daily operation — not another sales pitch.
$899 + tax POS package  •  $7,500 restaurant Odoo ERP implementation
We know this is not just about software
A restaurant owner carries pressure that a normal POS sales conversation usually ignores.

The hard part is not taking payment.
The hard part is controlling the business.
Receipts pile up. Inventory does not match sales. Managers answer questions manually. Delivery apps create reconciliation work. Staff training repeats again and again.
So our first job is to listen before showing screens.
We start in your shoes, then build the system around how your restaurant really works.
We ask about your current process first.
We identify where money and time are leaking.
We show only the screens that solve your problem.
We train your staff so the system is actually used.

This is not “buy our POS.”
This is “let’s make the restaurant easier to control.”
What usually hurts inside a restaurant operation
Most owners do not need more technology. They need fewer blind spots.
Can I trust the daily number?
Why does stock not match sales?
Where do orders get delayed or lost?
What should we reorder before it is too late?
Can I see the restaurant from home?
Front of house: fast, clean, easy for staff
The POS should reduce pressure during rush hours, not create new confusion.
The POS handles what happens at the counter.
Kitchen flow: fewer missed tickets, fewer arguments
The system should make the team calmer when the restaurant is busy.
No shouting. No lost tickets. Orders move cleanly from server to kitchen.
Server order → kitchen screen → preparation status → payment → inventory movement
Behind the POS: Odoo ERP connects the business
The $7,500 implementation builds the operating system behind the restaurant.
Inventory and purchasing: stop guessing what to buy
When sales and stock connect, purchasing becomes less reactive.

Low-stock alerts
Suggested purchase list
Variance report
Goal: know what is low, what is moving, and what needs to be ordered before it becomes a crisis.
Owner view: see the restaurant without being trapped inside it
The owner should not need five phone calls to know what happened today.
Owner view: sales, labor, inventory, purchasing, finance
At 11 PM, you should be able to see sales, labor, food cost, voids, discounts, and low-stock alerts.
Labor and permissions: control without micromanaging
Different roles need different access. The system should protect the owner and guide the staff.
Daily sales, shift close, inventory adjustments
Fewer “who changed this?” problems. More accountability.
Food cost and leakage: measure the hidden losses
A restaurant can be busy and still leak profit quietly.
Owner view: sales, labor, inventory, purchasing, finance
One system takes orders. The other connects the restaurant business.
The POS records transactions. The ERP turns those transactions into control.
Implementation roadmap: we do not disappear after payment
The value comes from setup, training, testing, and making sure your team can actually use it.
We train the real people who will touch the system every day: owner, manager, cashier, kitchen, and back office.
What we need from you to make this successful
A smooth project needs your restaurant knowledge. We bring the technical system; you bring the real operation.
Reports you want to see every day
We do not expect you to become technical. We translate your operation into the system.
The decision is not “Do I need another system?”
The better question is: “Do I want a smoother restaurant with better control?”
Stay with separate tools, manual checks, and after-hours guesswork.
Or build one connected flow: order → kitchen → payment → inventory → purchasing → reports.
Our recommendation: start with POS setup and ERP discovery.

Let’s make the restaurant
easier to run.

1. Confirm POS package: $899 + tax
2. Schedule ERP discovery
3. Collect menu / inventory / vendor information
4. Start setup, testing, and staff training
The goal is not more software. The goal is a smoother business.
